name: Trypsin + Chymotrypsin
meta: Trypsin: Proteolytic enzyme; Chymotrypsin: Proteolytic enzyme
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Trypsin: Schedule H –
prescription only; Chymotrypsin: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to yellowish-white crystalline or amorphous powder.
White to yellowish-white crystalline or amorphous powder.

Trypsin: Named in 1876 by German physiologist Wilhelm Kühne (from Greek 'thrýpto' – 'I break'); obtained from bovine or porcine pancreas. First approval/introduction: Pharmaceutical use of pancreatic proteases since the mid-20th century. Chymotrypsin: Formed from pancreatic chymotrypsinogen; combinations with trypsin are expressed in Armour units of enzymatic activity. First approval/introduction: Ophthalmic use (zonulolysis in cataract surgery) and oral anti-inflammatory use since the 1950s–60s.
The two pancreatic proteases act synergistically to break down inflammatory exudate and fibrin, reducing swelling and accelerating healing.

Trypsin Serine protease that hydrolyses proteins in inflammatory exudate and fibrin deposits, reducing oedema and accelerating resolution of inflammation and haematoma. Receptor / target profile: Cleaves peptide bonds on the carboxyl side of lysine and arginine; degrades fibrin and inflammatory debris.

Chymotrypsin Pancreatic serine protease with anti-inflammatory and anti-oedematous effect; combined with trypsin to enhance fibrinolytic and proteolytic action. Receptor / target profile: Cleaves peptide bonds after large hydrophobic residues (tyrosine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, leucine).
Small fraction absorbed intact; binds alpha-1-antitrypsin and alpha-2-macroglobulin
Summary: Enteric-coated; a fraction is absorbed intact from the intestine and bound to alpha-2-macroglobulin.
Summary: Enteric-coated; partial absorption from intestine.
Post-operative and post-traumatic inflammation and oedema
Abscesses and infected wounds (adjunct to antibiotics)
